sources.title: Broadcasters, services, and their distribution
sources.notes: **S01. [Broadcasters, services, and their distribution](https://alpha60-devops.github.io/alpha60-results-sports/docs/world-cup-ott-vendors.html).** Existing sports report and the publication destination for the broadcast comparison and rights valuation.

sources.title: language-geography page
sources.notes: **S02. [language-geography page](https://alpha60-devops.github.io/alpha60-results-sports/docs/world-cup-distro-en-es-fr.html).** Existing language evidence and the published French/Spanish map section. Full-country table totals differ from cropped map totals.

sources.title: Hollywood Reporter article
sources.notes: **S03. [Hollywood Reporter article](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/world-cup-final-tv-ratings-fox-telemundo-1236652686/).** User-supplied reporting lead. Full article unavailable: HTTP 402; no inaccessible content is quoted or assumed.

sources.title: FOX release, July 21
sources.notes: **S04. [FOX release, July 21](https://www.foxsports.com/stories/presspass/fifa-world-cup-2026-final-etches-place-record-books-most-watched-soccer-telecast-u-s-history).** Primary broadcaster release, July 21, 2026, citing Nielsen. Governs the FOX final and tournament-average inputs.

sources.title: NBCUniversal release, July 21
sources.notes: **S05. [NBCUniversal release, July 21](https://www.nbcuniversal.com/article/telemundo-and-peacock-redefine-soccer-fandom-us-record-breaking-audiences-spanish-language-coverage).** Primary NBCUniversal release, July 21, 2026. National TAD includes streaming; local-station measures have different universes and reach qualifiers.

sources.title: AP report, July 21
sources.notes: **S06. [AP report, July 21](https://apnews.com/article/444951fd3ad6a19a8a1e1fabed868181).** Earlier AP report, July 21, 2026; its preliminary Spanish figure is retained as a revision, not mixed with the later NBCU value.

sources.title: Nielsen methodology announcement
sources.notes: **S07. [Nielsen methodology announcement](https://www.nielsen.com/news-center/2025/nielsen-out-of-home-measurement-now-covers-100-of-the-united-states/).** Primary measurement notice, February 2025: expanded U.S. out-of-home coverage changes historical comparability.

sources.title: Bell Media
sources.notes: **S08. [Bell Media](https://www.bellmedia.ca/the-lede/press/bell-media-smashes-records-with-canadas-biggest-fifa-world-cup-ever-as-fifa-world-cup-2026-reaches-more-than-30-million-canadians-on-tsn-rds-ctv-noovo-and-crave/).** Primary Canadian broadcaster release, July 21, 2026, citing preliminary Numeris and separate internal streaming data.

sources.title: RTVE
sources.notes: **S09. [RTVE](https://amp.rtve.es/rtve/20260722/mundial-2026-alcanza-3843-millones-espectadores-unicos-rtve/17165132.shtml).** Primary Spanish broadcaster release, July 22, 2026, citing Fifty5Blue and distinct digital measures; limited to RTVE coverage.

sources.title: Groupe M6
sources.notes: **S10. [Groupe M6](https://www.groupem6.fr/fr/bilan-exceptionnel-pour-la-coupe-du-monde-2026-sur-m6-et-m6/).** Primary French broadcaster release, July 21, 2026: Médiamétrie/Médiamat plus internal M6+ data.

sources.title: ITV
sources.notes: **S11. [ITV](https://www.itv.com/presscentre/media-releases/itvs-fifa-world-cup-2026-england-match-coverage-peaks-154-million-viewers).** Primary UK broadcaster release, June 18, 2026. BARB specification still needed; the cited match predates Alpha60 sampling.

sources.title: Globo
sources.notes: **S12. [Globo](https://ge.globo.com/futebol/copa-do-mundo/noticia/2026/07/21/globo-alcanca-1427-milhoes-de-pessoas-durante-a-copa-do-mundo-de-2026.ghtml).** Broadcaster-reported Brazilian tournament reach, July 21, 2026. Measurement vendor and deduplication remain unresolved.

sources.title: Claro Sports, July 8
sources.notes: **S13. [Claro Sports, July 8](https://www.clarosports.com/futbol/mundial-2026/la-mayor-audiencia-del-siglo-mexico-vs-inglaterra-rompe-todos-los-records-con-60-millones-de-espectadores/).** Secondary Mexico benchmark, July 8, 2026. The roughly 60 million claim lacks an established metric/provider; excluded from governed comparisons.

sources.title: Earlier contract reporting
sources.notes: **S14. [Earlier contract reporting](https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/lifestyle/fox-telemundo-set-us500m-windfall-2026-world-cup).** Bloomberg report republished by The Business Times, May 30, 2017. Describes fee bases and conditional hosting bonuses; does not establish final cash paid.

sources.title: Contemporary fee reporting
sources.notes: Secondary reporting lead retained from the research plan. The accessible follow-up extract did not expose the fee amounts; the published calculations instead use sources 19 and 31–33.

sources.title: FT original, access limited
sources.notes: Subscription-limited underlying reporting lead; not used as independently inspected evidence of a contract or fee allocation.

sources.title: Netflix's current coverage scope
sources.notes: **S17. [Netflix's current coverage scope](https://www.netflix.com/tudum/features/fifa-womens-world-cup-2027).** Primary Netflix viewing information, updated August 21, 2026. Confirms Brazil dates, 64 matches, U.S./Canada territories and announced languages.

sources.title: FIFA's original U.S. agreement
sources.notes: **S18. [FIFA's original U.S. agreement](https://legal.fifa.com/tournament-organisation/commercial/media-releases/fifa-netflix-historic-broadcast-deal-2027-2031-womens-world-cup).** Primary FIFA announcement, December 20, 2024. Original U.S. deal includes Puerto Rico, all languages, 2027 and 2031; no fee disclosed.

sources.title: Reported Netflix price
sources.notes: **S19. [Reported Netflix price](https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2026/jul/29/netflix-is-paying-200-million-for-2027-womens-worl/).** Vanessa Perdomo report republished by The Spokesman-Review, July 29, 2026. Reports $200 million for 2027 U.S./Canada rights from unnamed sources; Netflix declined comment; 2031 price unknown.

sources.title: Historical Women's World Cup averages
sources.notes: **S20. [Historical Women's World Cup averages](https://www.sportsmediawatch.com/2023/08/womens-world-cup-viewership-down-big-early-timeslots-uswnt-exit/).** Sports Media Watch, August 2023. Historical FOX/FS1 averages for the 2019 and 2023 women’s tournaments; differences in schedule, format and team progress limit comparison.

sources.title: NBCUniversal · final tournament fixture table
sources.notes: Nielsen Big Data + Panel, Live+Same Day, match-window TAD; Adobe Analytics. Updated Mexico–England 23.2M. Streaming is included in TAD, not additional.

sources.title: Match TV · tournament audience report
sources.notes: Mediascope Russia. Ratings: men 14–59; reach: all people 4+. Includes separate live and repeat reach. Do not convert rating percentages into average people.

sources.title: CCTV · 2026 tournament report
sources.notes: CSM 35-city audience share. Cross-media contact and video-view totals are repeated exposures, not unique people.

sources.title: M6 · first-half financial results
sources.notes: July 29 financial release gives France–Spain 20.3M consolidated J+28, or J+7 when J+28 unavailable (footnote 9), versus July 21 release 20.2M at July 20. Keep the July 21 pair together for the same publication vintage.

sources.title: FOX · tournament press index
sources.notes: Mexico–England 21.742M, Mexico–Ecuador 10.430M. Fixture-level measurement details less complete than NBCU table.

sources.title: Sports Media Watch · USA–Belgium revision
sources.notes: 33.09M includes pre-match coverage; do not treat as match-only window.

sources.title: Nielsen Korea result reported by JoyNews24
sources.notes: Secondary report: JTBC final 3.4% nationwide pay-TV households. Reported combined 6.8% uses different broadcaster household universes; excluded from person-audience comparisons.

sources.title: TRT · 2026 tournament coverage announcement
sources.notes: Distribution context only. No verified comparable 2026 final audience extracted.

sources.title: IMG · Netflix 2027 production appointment
sources.notes: Production responsibility verified; contract cost undisclosed.

sources.title: NBC Sports · earlier Mexico–England audience
sources.notes: Earlier Telemundo 23.1M; superseded in July 21 tournament table by 23.2M.

sources.title: WSJ report reproduced by interviewee John Kosner
sources.notes: Reports FOX $485M and Telemundo $600M for packages including 2023 women and 2026 men. Reports Netflix $300M for 2027+2031 US rights. Conflicts in scope with later $200M 2027 US+Canada report; never subtract across scopes to infer 2031 price.

sources.title: Reuters · broadcaster fees and audience
sources.notes: Reports approximate $485M FOX and $600M Comcast rights packages including the World Cup. Not a disclosed contract or standalone allocation.

sources.title: MediaPost · US rights estimates
sources.notes: Estimates $485M English and $600M Spanish for 2026; use alongside conflicting bundle descriptions, not as audited contract prices.

sources.title: AP via NBC Dallas · tournament average and preliminary final
sources.notes: FOX 7.737M average across 104 broadcasts on FOX, FS1 and Tubi. Earlier Telemundo final 22.6M is superseded by the NBCU July 21 TAD 23.9M.
